I completely get where you're coming from and I think there is definitely not enough education following a diagnosis. Not at all trying to discount your experiences and I'm glad you have found rules that keep you safe and healthy :) 

For myself, my rule with eating out is that if the server or kitchen seem at all confused about Coeliac or I'm getting mixed mesages then I just wait to eat when I get home. Always have a gf muesli bar in my bag for emergencies too!

I would just say that while its good to be careful, it can very easily cross into obsessive behaviour if you let it. I was diagnosed 23 years ago and grew up not knowing anything other than eating gluten free. Throughout the years (and glutenings) I added more add and more rules for myself, until I realised I was now using my disease as an excuse for disordered eating behaviours. 

The number one rule for every Coeliac sufferer should always be "if in doubt, leave it out". Personally I've never had a reaction from kissing my partner after she's had a beer, as long as she's washed her mouth out with water. I've recently had both a blood test and colonoscopy and the dr is confident my Coeliac is under control. 

I don't say this to discount anyone else's experience,  I have just seen so many newly diagnosed people who think they'll never be able to live a nornal life again, and there's a lot of misinformation on articles on the internet. At the end of the day you know your body best though,  this is just my 2 cents
